sentence: This project studies how joined nanobody proteins that target virus-infected cells or tumor cells bring antibodies to those cells and remove them.
This project develops machine learning tools to track the behavior of mice that model Alzheimer's disease and to measure subtle changes in thinking.
This project studies how a brain region called the fan-shaped body turns odor cues into movements in adult Drosophila.
This project tries to find out how nerve cell changes in a brain circuit link to maternal care and stress responses after birth.
This project tries to find out how arginine helps Staphylococcus aureus bacteria survive antibiotic treatment, using mouse infections, tissue culture and imaging.
This project builds machine learning and network methods to study how chemicals from food affect flare-ups of lung disease.
This project studies the structure of viruses with double-stranded RNA to understand how they copy themselves and package their genome.
This project tests whether the drug semaglutide, alone or with anti-amyloid antibodies, works better against Alzheimer's disease in mouse models.
This project tries to find out how a muscle protein called myosin-binding protein C controls the exchange of myosin molecules in cardiac muscle.
This project studies how RNA-binding proteins and small RNAs in germ granules control gene expression and germ cell development.
This project builds imaging measures of muscle, fat, bone and brain to support research on physical function and disability.
This project studies a blood test that measures cancer cell-free DNA to look for many types of cancer at once.
This project studies how microbial cells, especially those that cause human disease, carry out basic metabolic processes.
This project studies how deep brain stimulation changes single neuron activity in mice and compares it with brain signals in patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder.
This project tests how patterns of dopamine release in the brain carry reward and other learning signals, using imaging in an odor-guided choice task.
This project uses microscopy to watch stem cells in the skin of live animals and find how they keep tissue in balance.
This project builds and tests a self-report tool that helps young people with variations in sex traits describe their care needs.
This project studies how the cancer osteosarcoma spreads and how the tumor surroundings drive that spread.
This project studies how an imbalance of microbes triggers immune activity during glottic wound healing after intubation injury, using human samples and mice.
